title: It Is Good to Draw Near to God

verses.text: Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
They have no struggle in their death; their bodies are well-fed.
They are free of the burdens others carry; they are not afflicted like other men.
Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.
From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.
They mock and speak with malice; with arrogance they threaten oppression.
They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut across the earth.
So their people return to this place and drink up waters in abundance.
The wicked say, "How can God know? Does the Most High have knowledge?"
Behold, these are the wicked— always carefree as they increase their wealth.
Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure; in innocence I have washed my hands.
For I am afflicted all day long and punished every morning.
If I had said, "I will speak this way," then I would have betrayed Your children.
When I tried to understand all this, it was troublesome in my sight
until I entered God's sanctuary; then I discerned their end.
Surely You set them on slick ground; You cast them down into ruin.
How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors!
Like one waking from a dream, so You, O Lord, awaken and despise their form.
When my heart was grieved and I was pierced within,
I was senseless and ignorant; I was a brute beast before You.
Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand.
You guide me with Your counsel, and later receive me in glory.
Whom have I in heaven but You? And on earth I desire no one besides You.
My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
Those far from You will surely perish; You destroy all who are unfaithful to You.
But as for me, it is good to draw near to God. I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, that I may proclaim all Your works.

context.author: Asaph, one of David’s chief musicians; his family led Temple singing for centuries (Ezra 2:41). Book Three (Psalms 73-89) opens with eleven psalms of Asaph (73-83), several of which mourn the fall of Jerusalem or of the northern kingdom, so many were written or adapted by later members of his guild.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, in times of national crisis
context.setting: Book Three opens with a confession: “Surely God is good to Israel… But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled… For I envied the arrogant when I saw the prosperity of the wicked” (vv.1-3). They are healthy, proud, violent and carefree (vv.4-12). “Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure” (v.13). Asaph could not make sense of it “until I entered God’s sanctuary; then I discerned their end” (v.17): they stand on slippery ground and are swept away (vv.18-20). He admits he was “a brute beast” (v.22). “Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand. You guide me with Your counsel, and later receive me in glory. Whom have I in heaven but You?… My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever” (vv.23-26). “It is good to draw near to God” (v.28).
context.custom: The sanctuary was where worshipers heard God’s word and saw the sacrifices, reminders of judgment and grace. Necklaces and fine clothes (v.6) were marks of wealth and status. “Portion” (v.26) was the share of land a family inherited; the Levites had no land, only God (Numbers 18:20), and Asaph was a Levite.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 74 mourns the destruction of God’s sanctuary.
context.timelineBible: Jesus’ parable of the rich man and Lazarus turns the prosperity of the wicked upside down (Luke 16:19-25). Paul wrote, “I count all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ” (Philippians 3:8). Jeremiah asked the same question: “Why does the way of the wicked prosper?” (Jeremiah 12:1), and so did Job (Job 21:7).

gospelParallels.note: Everything is loss compared to knowing Christ.

Why do the wicked live on?

overview.summary: Asaph nearly lost his faith envying the prosperous wicked, until in God’s sanctuary he saw their end and realized that God Himself is his portion forever.
overview.settingLine: Envy outside, clarity inside the sanctuary.

archaeology.t: Gold and silver jewelry from Iron Age tombs and hoards.

overview.discussion: Things changed when Asaph “entered God’s sanctuary” (v.17). Where do I go to see things from God’s point of view?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-80 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: Asaph
overview.audience: God, and those tempted to envy
